question: Your extraction system automated high-confidence extractions after a labeled validation set showed 96% overall accuracy. Handwritten receipts make up 4% of the documents. Weeks later, the downstream accounting system finds that many date fields from handwritten receipts contain wrong values. What most likely explains why the pre-automation validation missed this problem?

options.text: The receipts were processed through the Message Batches API, whose asynchronous processing lowers extraction accuracy compared to synchronous calls.
options.reason: The Message Batches API trades latency for 50% cost savings; it does not lower extraction accuracy, so it cannot explain the missed segment errors.

options.text: The validation reported only aggregate accuracy, so strong results on common document types hid poor date accuracy in the small handwritten receipt segment.
options.reason: Aggregate metrics can mask poor performance on specific document types or fields, which is why accuracy must be validated by document type and field before automating.

options.text: The extraction prompt lacked few-shot examples for handwritten receipts, so the model could not interpret their date formats reliably.
options.reason: This might explain why the errors occur, but it does not explain why validation missed them; only a per-segment accuracy analysis would have revealed the weak segment.

options.text: The JSON schema was used without strict mode, so syntax errors in the date fields passed through validation unnoticed.
options.reason: The dates are wrong values, which are semantic errors; strict schemas eliminate syntax errors but cannot catch semantic errors, and this does not explain the validation gap.
